title: Dark web crimes - the jurisdiction challenge for Indian police
p1:
What happens when a cybercriminal sitting thousands of kilometres away targets someone in India?

Which country's police should investigate? And under whose laws should the offender be prosecuted?

This is one of the biggest challenges Indian law enforcement faces when dealing with dark web crimes.
p2:
A common misconception is that crimes committed on the dark web are beyond the reach of Indian police.

That's not entirely true.

The real difficulty is jurisdiction — determining which country's authorities have the legal power to investigate, collect evidence, and prosecute an offender.

A criminal may operate from one country, use servers located in another, receive payments through cryptocurrency, and target victims in India.
p3:
This creates a complicated investigation involving multiple legal systems and international cooperation.

Indian police can investigate offences affecting victims in India under applicable Indian laws, including the Information Technology Act, 2000. However, identifying an offender, obtaining digital evidence from foreign platforms, and securing cooperation from overseas authorities can take considerable time.

Here's the surprising part: identifying where a crime happened online can be just as challenging as identifying who committed it.

For investigators, international cooperation is often as important as technical expertise.
conclusion: Should India strengthen international cybercrime cooperation to make dark web investigations faster and more effective? Or should stronger domestic investigative powers be the priority? Share your perspective.
